title: An Efficient Subgraph GNN with Provable Substructure Counting Power

problem.claim: The work investigates improving GNN representation power through substructure counting.

gap.claim: Subgraph GNNs have significant computational and memory costs despite identifying various substructures.

contributions.claim: The authors demonstrate that distance to rooted nodes in subgraphs is key to increasing substructure-counting power.
The authors introduce precomputed structural embeddings that encode distance information to avoid repeatedly applying GNNs across all subgraphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments show the proposed model retains the counting power of subgraph GNNs while achieving significantly faster performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies GNN representation power through substructure counting.
Subgraph GNNs augment graph representations by processing many subgraphs but incur substantial computational and memory costs.
The paper asks whether GNNs can count substructures efficiently and provably.
The authors identify rooted-node distances as important, encode them in precomputed embeddings, and report retained counting power with faster performance.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact model architecture.
The abstract does not report datasets, metrics, or numerical speedups.
The abstract does not define the precise theoretical counting guarantee.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
